title: 'History is repeating': Michael Burry says it's time to read about Enron
excerpt: Michael Burry of "The Big Short" fame recommended "The Smartest Guys in the Room" as he sees parallels between Enron's rise and fall and the AI boom.
content_html:
By Theron Mohamed

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Looking for a beach read this summer? Michael Burry of "The Big Short" fame has a recommendation.

In a late Tuesday post on X, Burry shared a link to an Amazon listing for "The Smartest Guys in the Room: The Amazing Rise and Scandalous Fall of Enron."

"History is repeating," he wrote. "Time to read this one again, or for the first time."

The business classic, written by investigative journalists Bethany McLean and Peter Elkind and first published in 2003, tells the story of Enron, the fraudulent energy titan that collapsed into what was then the biggest bankruptcy in US history in December 2001.

The energy supplier and trading powerhouse used a series of financial tricks to perpetrate its fraud. It used mark-to-market accounting to book the entire projected value of long-term contracts as immediate profit. It also used special-purpose entities and circular financing deals to keep huge debts off its balance sheet, manufacture earnings, and inflate its stock price.

Former Goldman Sachs CEO Lloyd Blankfein said in his recent memoir that Enron was at one point the "bane of my existence." Goldman couldn't figure out how Enron was ostensibly making so much more money in energy and commodity markets, and profitably trading bandwidth.

"As we learnt later, Enron was an enormous fraud," Blankfein wrote. "It was accumulating unhedged, long-dated risk that it marked at levels it could trade out at."

Burry didn't elaborate on what he meant by "history is repeating," but it was likely in reference to his frequent criticisms of big AI companies in recent months.

He's said they're overspending on microchips and data centers, dragging out depreciation to flatter their earnings, striking circular financing deals to fuel the buzz around AI, and using off-balance-sheet structures to disguise leverage and risk.

Burry didn't immediately respond to a request for comment from Business Insider.

Jim Chanos, another short-seller known for spotting the red flags at Enron and betting it would crumble, has also questioned whether the tech titans pumping hundreds of billions of dollars into AI infrastructure will see a return on their money.

Burry, whose contrarian wager against the mid-2000s housing bubble was chronicled in the book and movie "The Big Short," pivoted from running a hedge fund to writing about his personal portfolio on Substack late last year.

He's bet against a raft of major AI players in recent months, including Nvidia, Palantir, Oracle, Nebius, and Micron.

Burry has raised this specter before, suggesting after the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank in early 2023: "It is possible today we found our Enron."

正在寻找今年夏天的海滩读物吗？ 《大空头》成名的迈克尔·伯里有一个推荐。

在周二晚间 X 上的一篇帖子中，伯里分享了一个亚马逊列表的链接，内容是“房间里最聪明的人：安然公司的惊人崛起和丑闻倒塌”。

“历史正在重演，”他写道。 “是时候再读一遍这篇文章了，或者说是第一次读这篇文章。”

这部商业经典著作由调查记者贝瑟尼·麦克莱恩 (Bethany McLean) 和彼得·埃尔金德 (Peter Elkind) 撰写，于 2003 年首次出版，讲述了安然公司的故事。安然公司是一家欺诈性的能源巨头，于 2001 年 12 月陷入了当时美国历史上最大的破产案。

这家能源供应商和贸易巨头使用了一系列金融伎俩来实施欺诈。 它使用按市值计价的会计方法将长期合同的全部预计价值记为即时利润。 它还利用特殊目的实体和循环融资交易将巨额债务从资产负债表中剔除，制造盈利并抬高股价。

高盛前首席执行官劳埃德·布兰克费恩在他最近的回忆录中表示，安然一度是“我存在的祸根”。 高盛无法弄清楚安然表面上是如何在能源和大宗商品市场以及带宽交易上赚得如此多的钱的。

“正如我们后来了解到的那样，安然公司是一个巨大的骗局，”布兰克费恩写道。 “它正在积累未对冲的长期风险，并将其标记为可以交易的水平。”

伯里没有详细说明“历史正在重演”的含义，但这很可能是指他最近几个月对大型人工智能公司的频繁批评。

他表示，他们在微芯片和数据中心上超支，拖累折旧以抬高收入，达成循环融资协议以推动人工智能的热潮，并利用表外结构来掩盖杠杆和风险。

伯里没有立即回应《商业内幕》的置评请求。

另一位卖空者吉姆·查诺斯 (Jim Chanos) 因发现安然公司的危险信号并押注该公司将崩溃而闻名，他也质疑这些向人工智能基础设施投入数千亿美元的科技巨头是否会获得回报。

伯里在《大空头》一书和电影中记录了他对 2000 年代中期房地产泡沫的逆势押注，他从经营一家对冲基金转向去年年底在 Substack 上撰写个人投资组合。

近几个月来，他做空了许多主要人工智能公司，包括 Nvidia、Palantir、Oracle、Nebius 和 Micron。

伯里之前曾提出过这种担忧，他在 2023 年初硅谷银行倒闭后表示：“今天我们有可能找到了我们的安然公司。”
